episodes.178840: The combination of a strong upper ridge over the region which provided for much above normal temperatures across the area and an easterly flow over central California  continued to provide for mid and upper level moisture to stream into the area. With moisture and instability sufficient for convection to take place, scattered thunderstorms broke out during the afternoon over the Sierra Nevada and Tehachapi Mountains as well as across the Kern County Deserts. One thunderstorm in the desert produced heavy rainfall which resulted in debris flow flooding over a portion of U.S. 395 near Randsburg, while another thunderstorm produced wind gusts above 60 mph in Ridgecrest.
episodes.178855: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over far northwestern Crook County, producing hail to half dollar size near the Montana border.
episodes.179009: Lightning struck and killed a 24 year-old man while he was working on a roof in Volusia County, causing him to fall off of the roof.
episodes.179010: A thunderstorm produced severe hail and a severe wind gust in Saint Cloud.
episodes.179287: The combination of a surface low and deep-layer trough northwest of Puerto Rico created a band of convergence across the islands. This produced numerous showers and thunderstorms across the eastern sections of Puerto Rico on May 22, 2023, which resulted in river flooding in Naguabo.
episodes.179296: Thunderstorms with heavy rain and gusty winds developed over the area.  A few reports of trees down were received, and rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches resulted in reports of minor flooding.
episodes.179297: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms produced pockets of heavy rain across the area.  Amounts of 3 to 5 inches in resulted in minor flooding in a few areas.
episodes.179351: After a cold front brought cooler and drier conditions on the 20th, moisture returned to the region on the afternoon of the 21st which fueled scattered showers and thunderstorms. An increase in the wind fields aloft allowed for some storms to produce gusty surface winds. One storm did produce a 59 mph wind gust near the Hale/Floyd County line.
episodes.179352: Another afternoon of severe thunderstorms occurred across the region on the 22nd. Severe thunderstorms dropped hail as large as two inches in diameter in several locations. The widespread thunderstorm activity organized into a larger complex of thunderstorms that produced heavy rain and severe wind gusts as it accelerated southeastward through the Rolling Plains during the evening. The bowing line of thunderstorms generated a peak wind gust of 80 mph as it moved across the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Aspermont (Stonewall County). These severe winds also caused minor damage in and around Aspermont.
episodes.179406: Evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce wind damage near Lake Alfred in Polk County.
episodes.179448: Thunderstorms developed across western Montana ahead of an approaching trough. High amounts of atmospheric moisture and slow storm motion contributed to a flash flood threat, especially over recent burn scars. A few storms produced quarter size hail.
episodes.179635: Thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening of May 21, some of them approaching severe strength. An approaching trough helped create lift for storms, and favorable CAPE and shear profiles led to the severe risk. A severe thunderstorm watch was issued for Idaho and Clearwater counties.
episodes.179637: Another afternoon of thunderstorm development resulted in a severe thunderstorm near Helmville and Ovando.
episodes.180278: A front stalled across the local forecast area and served as a focus for localized heavy rainfall in diurnally enhanced sea breeze convection.

episodes.180389: A strong upper level trough moved into the region with favorable ingredients for strong thunderstorms. Widespread severe thunderstorms brought severe hail and winds to the region, causing minor damage to structures, numerous flight delays, and a capsized boat on Lake Lowell.
episodes.180498: A weak pressure pattern existed over the Florida Keys as low pressure developed northeast of the Bahamas and high pressure ridging was in place over the central Gulf of Mexico.  Waterspouts developed in Florida Bay near Marathon.
episodes.180548: Abnormal late-May moisture and weak instability fueled scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Flash flooding and isolated severe weather occurred.
episodes.180549: Abnormal late-May moisture and weak instability fueled scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Several storms produced high winds.
episodes.180679: A pattern developed by late May with sufficient moisture and forcing to yield scattered showers and thunderstorms almost every day, generally from the afternoon on into the early evening hours. Some of these storms were strong, yielding damaging wind gusts and hail. Additionally, a road washout was reported as a result of continued spring runoff from the prior winter's record snowfall.
episodes.180790: Early in the afternoon on the 22nd, multiple storms developed across the south central to southeastern Texas Panhandle. Some of these storms produced hail up to 1.5 and some heavy rainfall causing flooding in Gray County. Later in the afternoon a supercell developed over Beaver County in the Oklahoma Panhandle with another supercell forming in southwest Kansas before moving into the central and eastern portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. These storms were in a very good environment for hail growth leading to reports of 2.5 diameter hail, especially once they got into Ochilltree County in the Texas Panhandle as they moved south to southeast. Some flooding was reported in Beaver County as well due to the initial storm then the Kansas storm training over the same area with heavy rainfall rates.
episodes.180791: Early in the afternoon on the 22nd, multiple storms developed across the south central to southeastern Texas Panhandle. Some of these storms produced hail up to 1.5 and some heavy rainfall causing flooding in Gray County. Later in the afternoon a supercell developed over Beaver County in the Oklahoma Panhandle with another supercell forming in southwest Kansas before moving into the central and eastern portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. These storms were in a very good environment for hail growth leading to reports of 2.5 diameter hail, especially once they got into Ochilltree County in the Texas Panhandle. Some flooding was reported in Beaver County as well due to the initial storm then the Kansas storm training over the same area with heavy rainfall rates.
episodes.180836: Heavy rain reported on 05/21 in Kearny County.
episodes.180837: A thunderstorm produced severe hail across portions of Seward County.
episodes.180868: The active weather pattern continued across the southern Great Plains. An active sub-tropical jet stream with embedded disturbances helped initiate thunderstorms off the higher elevations and along a dryline across the region. A few supercells produced large hail and damaging winds across the Permian Basin. A brief landspout was also reported with one thunderstorm.
episodes.180928: Incoming  trough off the Pacific Northwest coast flattened high pressure across the west allowing for increased potential for more widespread showers and thunderstorms through May 21 that continued into the early part of the following week.
episodes.180950: A prolonged period of well-below-average spring temperatures combined with an above-average winter snowpack created a dynamic breakup of the Yukon River. This resulted in numerous ice jams and snowmelt flooding on the Yukon River. Breakup flooding began on May 12th in eastern Alaska in Eagle and ended on June 3rd in the Yukon River delta at the Bering Sea coast at the community of Emmonak. The primary cause of this active flood year was a 1-2 week delay in breakup when compared to typical timing. April temperatures were well below normal, and when temperatures began to warm in early May, it melted the low-elevation snowpack quickly. Because of the relatively quick addition of snowmelt onto strong ice, the ice was more susceptible to jamming and floods. In addition to the late breakup, the snowpack this winter was 1 to 1.5 times greater than the climatological normal for interior and western Alaska. Significant ice jams and associated flooding on the Upper Yukon River resulted in large volumes of ice and water to move down into the Lower Yukon River.
episodes.181074: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms developed in the western combined OK and TX Panhandles during the afternoon of the 21st. Thunderstorm activity picked up going into the evening as it moved east across the area. Besides some heavy rainfall one of these storms produced hail up to 0.9 in diameter in the Oklahoma Panhandle.
episodes.181303: A slow moving thunderstorm brought heavy rain to the Russell Mountain Burn Scar. The rain and snow melt washed out area road.
episodes.181354: A passing upper-level trough and cold front produced a couple strong to severe T-storms over the eastern mountains aided by diurnal heating. The severe T-storm activity was focused in the Wallowa County area and produced up to 1.5 inch hail, locally gusty winds, and heavy downpours.
episodes.181365: An unusually cold spring kept snowpack intact and in place over the Copper River Basin into mid May.  Once temperatures started to warm, they did so quickly and rapidly melted snowpack in the basin.  An additional snow event later in May repeated the process creating multiple events where snowmelt would impact Glennallen and Old Edgerton Highway from Moose Creek snowmelt, and Gulkana and Sourdough areas along the Gulkana River.
episodes.181372: Strong thunderstorms brought small hail and winds to the Lake Pend Oreille area. Hail sizes with near 0.75. Wind gusts maxed near 30 MPH.
episodes.181703: An early monsoonal moisture push occurred during the middle of May across Southern California. The heaviest activity occurred in the High Desert, where several reports of flooding were documented. Hot and humid conditions also occurred region-wide.

On the lower Yukon River at Russian Mission, an ice jam formed downriver from Russian Mission near Marshall on May 21st. Major flooding began May 22nd with complete submersion of the airport runway, inundating 2-3 homes, and other miscellaneous structures. Additional homes and structures were completely surrounded by flood water for four days. The ice jam released on May 24th, which resulted in a gradual drop in water levels as the large volume of impounded water from the extensive lowland flooding between Holy Cross and Russian Mission drained. An ice jam flood warning was issued on May 22nd and was canceled on May 27th. Flood advisory products were continued until June 2nd.
